question: Can task-specific continuous prompt and verbalizer embeddings, trained against a frozen masked language model, match fine-tuning-like quality with a tiny number of trainable parameters?
hypothesis: We hypothesize that it is possible to find such prompts: extra tokens that exploit language model capabilities better than manually designed ones.
contributions: WARP: gradient-trained prompt and verbalizer embeddings in continuous space on a frozen MLM
81.6 GLUE test score with up to 25K trainable parameters
Manual-prompt initialization enabling few-shot results on CB and RTE with 32 examples, beating GPT-3
Storage analysis for serving many tasks from one frozen model

method.summary: Trainable prompt embeddings [P_1..P_K] are inserted before, between and after the input sentences together with a [MASK] token; the MLM head output at the mask (without decoder) is projected by trainable verbalizer embeddings [V_1..V_C] and trained with cross-entropy. Everything else in the pretrained model is frozen.
method.task: sentence and sentence-pair classification (GLUE, FewGLUE CB/RTE) via cloze reformulation

datasets.name: GLUE (9 tasks)
datasets.size: train sizes: MNLI 392702, QNLI 104743, QQP 363846, RTE 2490, SST 67349, MRPC 3668, CoLA 8551, STS-B 5749
datasets.split: dev for model selection and early stopping; test via GLUE server
datasets.preprocessing: WNLI always predicts majority label; STS-B scores clipped to [1,5]

datasets.name: FewGLUE CB and RTE
datasets.split: 20 runs each with 16 random train examples and the rest as dev for learning-rate choice; 20000 unlabeled examples not used

models.name: albert-xxlarge-v2
models.params: inferred: 255M, stated as roughly the same as PET/iPET

models.name: WARP
models.params: <25K trainable on GLUE; 1024 trainable per few-shot model
models.init_from: [MASK] embedding, or MNLI-trained prompts (RTE, MRPC, STS-B), or PVP token embeddings (few-shot)

training.objective: cross-entropy over verbalizer logits; MSE regression head for STS-B
training.optimizer: AdamW (huggingface), weight decay disabled; gradient normalized to 1.0
training.lr: per task from {1e-2,3e-3,1e-3,3e-4,1e-4,3e-5}; chosen 0.001 (MNLI, QNLI, RTE, MRPC, CoLA, STS-B), 0.0003 (QQP), 0.003 (SST-2)
training.batch_size: at most 8 examples and 1024 tokens per batch (Sec 3.2); Appendix says max 2048 tokens per batch
training.precision: mixed precision, lengths padded to multiples of 8
training.hardware: two Titan V and two RTX 3080 GPUs
training.compute: hyperparameter search roughly 4 days on two Titan V GPUs
training.wall_clock: WARP 2.5-3x faster per epoch than fine-tuning, 2x slower than frozen features
training.seeds: few-shot: 20 runs ensembled by majority vote; GLUE seeds not stated

other.batch_note: Sec 3.2 says 1024 tokens, Appendix A says 2048 tokens per batch; bucketing with padding noise 0.1

inference.samples: few-shot: ensemble of 20 WARP runs by majority vote
inference.prompting: GLUE: prompt tokens before, between, after sentences, [MASK] between sentences for pairs; WARP_init template [CLS] S1? [MASK]. S2! [SEP]

metrics.name: GLUE score / per-task metrics
metrics.definition: accuracy (SST-2, MNLI matched), Matthews corr (CoLA), F1 (QQP, MRPC), Pearson (STS-B); AVG over tasks

eval.protocol: Single-task training, early stopping and selection on dev set; test via leaderboard servers; Fig 4 shows median/min/max over 10 runs

prompts.purpose: WARP_init shared manual prompt for GLUE

evidence.quote: Each batch consists of examples containing at most 1024 tokens and 8 examples.

results.claim: WARP (RoBERTa) reaches GLUE test average 81.6 with under 25K trainable parameters, beating all submissions with up to 25M trainable parameters.
results.setup: roberta-large frozen, GLUE leaderboard test, <25K trainable params
results.quote: achieves 81.6 test score on the GLUE Leaderboard
results.note: Fully fine-tuned RoBERTa scores 88.1 and DeBERTa 90.8

results.claim: On dev sets WARP_20 averages 84.8 vs 88.9 for full fine-tuning.
Few-shot CB test: WARP_init (ALBERT, 32 examples) beats GPT-3 and PET but trails iPET.
results.setup: albert-xxlarge-v2, 32 training examples, ensemble of 20 runs, SuperGLUE test server
results.table: Table 3, test, row WARPinit (ALBERT), columns CB F1 / Acc.

results.claim: Few-shot RTE test accuracy of WARP_init is 69.1 vs GPT-3 69.0 and iPET 70.8.
results.table: Table 3, test, row WARPinit (ALBERT), column RTE Acc.

results.claim: With a single prompt token WARP gets 93.8% on SST-2 dev, above AutoPrompt's 91.2%.
results.quote: which allows WARP to get better performance with just a single prompt token (93.8%)

results.claim: Adding prompt tokens improves dev average monotonically from 72.4 (0 tokens) to 82.1 (8 tokens).
Manual-prompt initialization helps on small datasets: WARP_init RTE dev 80.1 vs 72.9 for WARP_8.
WARP is 2.5-3x faster per epoch than fine-tuning.
results.quote: WARP is 2.5-3 times faster than regular ﬁne-tuning

limits: Weak on CoLA (53.9 test) which authors attribute to difficulty of cloze reformulation
Learned prompt tokens are not interpretable
Few-shot results trail iPET, which uses 20000 unlabeled examples
Only classification/regression with encoders tested; autoregressive extension only footnoted
Test GLUE trails fully fine-tuned RoBERTa by 6.5 points
Seeds for GLUE runs not reported

terms.definition: Word-level Adversarial ReProgramming: learn task-specific word embeddings concatenated to the input to instruct a frozen language model

lineage.work: Adversarial reprogramming of neural networks (Elsayed et al.)
lineage.note: idea of trained input padding for a frozen network
discrete prompt search; WARP searches embedding space

lineage.work: Language models are few-shot learners (Brown et al.)
Parameter-efficient transfer learning for NLP (Houlsby et al.)
